goal_title: Book: Color and Composition — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in color became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence takes a thing the visitor has been walking through since the first hall and gives it conditions. It opens by gathering primitives, transformations and arrays into twenty-four painted columns, where one word in a rule decides what a colour is a function of: the object, the kind, the height, or the neighbour below. Then it moves the conditions one at a time: the light that reaches a surface (Flashlight), the body that wears the colour (Nails), the partition a rule imposes on a familiar outline (Rainbow), the field between the samples (Pillar), the address that keeps a value until it is overwritten (Grid), the surface that remembers by forgetting (Paint), and finally a wall that lets a view through but not a body, beside two models that turn colour into coordinates (Walls). The through-line is that a colour value never arrives alone; it has company (a surface, a light, a neighbour, a viewer, a memory), and the code gives a precise handle on the construction without accounting for the meeting. It hands the disco floor back to tiling with its rules intact and its palette changed.
holds: "A colour with company": the by_neighbour column's lesson ("A neighbour has become an input") returns in Grid ("The room where colour needed company has followed us here") and in Paint's turn to the Albers surround.

The array vocabulary carried in from array_tutorial: address, list, remainder. `i % stripe_colors.size()` (Context), "Its position in the list gives it a colour" (Rainbow), `(address.x + address.y) % palette.size()` (Grid).

One act of assignment at different targets: `m.albedo_color = c` (Context), `spot.light_color` (Flashlight), `material.albedo_color = colour` (Nails), `set_instance_color` (Grid). The reader learns to see the same line landing on different surfaces.
Geometry stays while colour changes: the arch's opening, the cube that still supports you, the 1.2 m doorway that stays when the panes go opaque. Each hall has its own "no new geometry" sentence.
The HSV thread: introduced at the Rainbow (only hue travels), varied at the Pillars (only saturation travels), compared at the Walls (RGB path versus HSV arc between the same endpoints).

Carried objects: the colour on the visitor's own hands from Nails onward (GameManager persists it into later halls), a swatch taken from the Pillar wall, and the disco floor itself, which Walls sends ahead and Pattern_Disco receives.
Every chapter closes with a question addressed to the next hall, and every opening answers it in its first lines ("In the previous room...", "At the pillars...", "At the grid...", "In Paint...").

hall_notes.note: Gathers primitives, transformations and arrays into sixteen chroma_stack columns and lets one word (the rule) decide what a colour is a function of; then eight color_dna_stack studies raise table-sized configurations to six and seven metres. Reads as two halls in one: the first half is the sequence's best teaching, the second half a catalogue with borrowed names, an internal identifier and the word DNA.

Four pickable lamps (red, green, blue, white aimed aside), a near-white board, a cube and a seven-sided sphere: the visitor moves the light and watches the patch of colour move with it. Reads cleanly; the code excerpt is small and true, and the "useful limit" paragraph is exemplary honesty about what RGB lamps do not calculate.

Two RGB boxes on labelled plinths colour the nails and skin of a giant hand, a petite hand and the visitor's own hands; the manicure becomes an assignment. Warm and quick, but the last third steps outside the headset to talk about VR and desktop.

A party room with a re-divisible arch (six, seven, forty-eight, two bands at one total width), confetti on entry and on demand, and HSV introduced through a "continuous" preset that is still forty-eight seams. The prose is generous and every number is right; the welcome on entry only fires for desktop and walker bodies.

Thirty-five pillars sample a continuous hue-by-saturation field the visitor can walk between, with a wall of twelve named sets as the other way of collecting. Shortest hall, tight, every number verified, and the swatch pickup carries a decision on to the next room.

A five-button console writes one of four inks to one of twenty-five floor addresses, and RULE rewrites the whole interior floor. The best-argued hall about what an address keeps and why the rule returns; one caption word leaks the toolchain.

An automatic painter and thirty pigment balls share a wet canvas that fades toward white; the surface remembers by becoming another image. Reads well and its excerpts match the source; it leans once on a hall three sequences back.

Forty coloured panes toggle glass/opaque while the doorways stay, then an RGB cube, an HSV cylinder and a sixteen-cube gradient compare ways of organising colour values. Three works, three clear regions, and an exact hand-over to Pattern_Disco.

stumbles: Color_Context_Placed: nearly twice the length of any other hall (1352 words against 476 to 796) and the heaviest load in the sequence: five rules, seven alphabets, four poses, four composed studies, then eight named studies, "the gallery's `ps07_kras_rainbow`" and "DNA". It is the first hall the visitor meets.

Color_Nails: "In VR, raise the hand moving with your controller..." and "On desktop, the giant and petite hands carry this comparison. In VR, your hands carry the chosen colours beyond the salon." The reader is in the headset; both sentences are written from outside it.

Color_Rainbow: the room's promised welcome ("Confetti opens above it... the room is pleased you arrived") never fires for a headset visitor: the trigger tests groups that XR Tools' PlayerBody does not carry (rainbow_celebration.gd:177; base.tscn:168; grid.tscn:47). Desktop and the museum walker get the confetti.

Color_Rainbow: a pick-up cube (x=2, z=3) and a catalyst pedestal offering the bracelet for a 45-second lease (x=12, z=3) flank the wall opposite the console, beside the teleporter; in the museum's first-row-to-last-row walk that wall is the door, so they are the first things seen. The chapter never mentions them, and the book first names the bracelet in later sequences.
Color_Grid_Pallet: the caption "the same cube still supports the walker" uses the project's probe and museum vocabulary; the visitor is not "the walker".

Color_Context_Placed: "at a camera height of 1.65 metres above its base" (a capture-rig fact) and "This is the gallery's `ps07_kras_rainbow`" (an internal identifier and a gallery the reader has not been told about) both surface in reader prose.

Color_Context_Placed: the blue circle / red square / yellow triangle is called "a choice in the code" when it is Kandinsky's 1923 Bauhaus questionnaire (chroma_stack.gd:30-31, 109-112). In a hall about associations that arrive with a colour, the strongest one is withheld.

Color_Walls: "Sixteen small cubes hold the intervening values": the sixteen include both endpoints (t = i/15, gradient_interpolator.gd:251), so fourteen intervene; the next paragraph ("t runs from zero to one across the sixteen samples") is right.

Color_Paint: "as the drawn line did in Trace" points three sequences back (Point_Trace) with no reminder of what was snapped there; the book does use "Trace" as that hall's name, so this is a memory demand rather than an error.

Color_Flashlight, Color_Nails, Color_Rainbow, Color_Walls: no `s` spawn cell, but an `sp` cell where the author evidently meant the spawn. `sp` is a score cube (a "0" label), and without `s` a standalone headset load starts at the floor centroid facing the interactables (GridSpawnComponent.gd:24-27), under the arch in Rainbow. The museum lane enters by passage and is untouched; the slip is systemic (603 of 2808 maps, 53 on the spine).

keep.quote: Nothing in a triangle requires yellow; here, yellow helps us recognise a relation someone has chosen to make.
If a Pride flag, a sweet wrapper or a fairground comes to mind, the array has not stored that memory. The arrangement meets something you bring.
Perhaps the surprising body here is the patch of colour. You cannot pick it up separately from the meeting that produces it.
The same programmed event can be a reward for obedience or an invitation that asks nothing of you; here you can repeat it without passing a test.
The gaps between columns contain possibilities that the collection has not put into a body. They are also where you can walk.
The rule did not return because the exception was impossible. It returned because you pressed a button that wrote across the floor again.
The surface remembers by becoming another image. It does not preserve a list of gestures that can be retrieved intact.
Your view took a route your body could not.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Tutorial_Disco closes: "Next, our familiar forms gather in coloured stacks. A stored value can assign a colour to a surface. What happens when that colour meets its neighbours?" Color_Context_Placed answers in its first lines ("On the disco floor, the positions stayed fixed while the pattern changed. Here, different choices stand beside one another") and the by_neighbour column turns the neighbour question into a rule. The disco chapter's "familiar forms" (block, sphere, wedge) are the exact alphabet of the first four columns.
reading.handover_out: Exact. Color_Walls closes: "Ahead, the disco floor returns in colour. Keep its arrangement and change its palette. Does the same pattern still invite the same movement?" Pattern_Disco opens "Do you recognise the floor in its new colours?", names the same twelve-by-twelve floor, console and sequencer (the map tokens are identical apart from `mode:colour`), summarises what Colour taught as "Brightness, contrast, neighbourhood and attention", and carries the movement question into its own @standalone_disco region. Nothing promised at the end of Walls is missing at the start of tiling.
reading_errors: Column count: the arc says 'twenty-four painted columns' and the Color_Context_Placed note says 'sixteen chroma_stack columns'. The map places 15 chroma_stack tokens (rows 6, 12, 18 and 26 hold 4+3+4+4) plus 8 color_dna_stack, i.e. 23 columns; the chapter's own arithmetic (four rule columns, three alphabets, four poses, four loosened stacks) agrees with 15. Same slip in task 3's evidence.

Color_Rainbow note: 'the welcome on entry only fires for desktop and walker bodies' is false. The XR PlayerBody is in the player_body group by its own scene (addons/godot-xr-tools/player/player_body.tscn:5), instanced without override at commons/scenes/base.tscn:168; rainbow_celebration.gd:149 masks its layer and :177 accepts the group.

Color_Rainbow note: 'confetti on entry' is a standalone-lane fact, not a museum one. The museum enters a map-authored hall at the tile's first row (ada_run/em_layout_walk.json Color_Rainbow first_row, with a 4-row vestibule before it; the walk finishes at the last row), and the WelcomePatch sits at local z 6.4 of a rainbow placed at row 13 (rainbow_celebration.gd:150), i.e. row ~19.9 of 26, past the arch (row ~11.5) and just before the exit. In the museum the burst comes at the end of the hall; the iteration's probe only saw it 'on arrival' because it teleported the walker to local z 9 first (doc/book/iterations/2026-09-23-rainbow-room-for-another/probe.gd:70-80). The chapter's 'Enter along the coloured centre path' has the same orientation problem.

'Every chapter closes with a question addressed to the next hall, and every opening answers it in its first lines' is overstated. Color_Pillar closes with an instruction ('Keep the spaces between these samples in mind.', final.md:37) and opens with no reference to the rainbow room at all; Flashlight's back-reference is at line 11, Rainbow's at line 13 and Walls's at line 26, not their first lines. Only Nails (line 3), Grid (line 7) and Paint (line 7) open with it.

Color_Nails note: 'the last third steps outside the headset to talk about VR and desktop' — the first device aside is line 13 of 43 (first third); only the desktop/VR pair at line 35 is in the last third.
Task 5's evidence says 15 final.md files carry footnote definitions; the count is 31. Not a summary error but a stale number in the task list.

dropped.title: Let the headset visitor trigger the welcome confetti
dropped.reason: The premise is false: the XR body carries the group. addons/godot-xr-tools/player/player_body.tscn:5 reads `[node name="PlayerBody" type="CharacterBody3D" groups=["player_body"]]`; commons/scenes/base.tscn:22 resolves ExtResource 16_3o0oe to that file and :168 instances it with no `groups=` override, so the instanced PlayerBody keeps `player_body` (groups in a PackedScene are applied on instantiate). rainbow_celebration.gd:149 masks 1<<19, which is the body's layer 524288 (player_body.tscn:8), and :177 accepts `player_body`, so the chain the task calls broken is complete: body_entered fires and _welcome celebrates. The reader cited line 8 of the very file that declares the group on line 5, and the comment at commons/artifacts/approach_scale/approach_scale.gd:357-358 ("the VR XRToolsPlayerBody in no group at all") is stale and is probably what misled them. The addon is gitignored (.gitignore:13 `/addons/*`), so the working-tree file is exactly what the headset export ships. Caveat: static verification only (Godot not started, as instructed); nothing in the chain depends on runtime state. The proposed code change would be harmless but is unnecessary, and the chapter's sentence keeps its promise.

tasks.title: Trim the DNA-stack region to what the visitor can test
tasks.spec:
[structure] Color_Context_Placed
Quote: “These choices have been saved: which forms, which proportions, which colours, and how the parts meet. The project often calls such a description DNA. tasks.title: Attribute the circle-blue, square-red, triangle-yellow rule
tasks.spec:
[footnote] Color_Context_Placed
Quote: “The cone and wedge share yellow. Their grouping is a choice in the code. Nothing in a triangle requires yellow; here, yellow helps us recognise a relation someone has chosen to make.”
Why: The by_shape assignment is Kandinsky's 1923 Bauhaus questionnaire and the five-piece alphabet follows Siedhoff-Buscher's Bauspiel, both named in the artifact's own header. The chapter's theme is the association that arrives with a colour before you measure it; here the strongest one is withheld, and "a choice in the code" reads as if the author of the code made it up.
Do: Add a footnote in the book's existing style after "someone has chosen to make": "[^kandinsky]: The assignment follows the questionnaire Wassily Kandinsky circulated at the Bauhaus in 1923 (circle blue, square red, triangle yellow); the stack's five-piece alphabet follows Alma Siedhoff-Buscher's Bauspiel (1923)."
Evidence: commons/artifacts/chroma_stack/chroma_stack.gd:30-31 ("after the questionnaire Kandinsky ran at the Bauhaus in 1923: circle blue, square red, triangle yellow"), :43 (Siedhoff-Buscher, Bauspiel), :109-112 and :123-128 (KIND_COLOR), :8 (relationships line); footnote convention: 15 final.md files carry [^id]: entries, e.g. commons/maps/Point_Trace/final.md:3 [^point-trace-klee].
